title: Frontiers: How Much Influencer Marketing Is Undisclosed? Evidence from Twitter
authors: Daniel Ershov; Yanting He; Stephan Seiler
package_mismatch_note: The archive under this suffix belongs to a different paper: ReadMe.txt and scripts concern a Pandora/SiriusXM ad-load experiment (subscriptions, listening hours, IV regressions of outcomes on realized ad load instrumented by treatment group, ML heterogeneous treatment effects, Pareto frontier of ad-load personalization) and ship only simulated data (01.simulateData.R, 02.simulatePanelData.R). No file mentions Twitter, influencers, sponsorship or disclosure.
eligible_reason: Not eligible. (i) Per the OpenAlex abstract, the paper uses a text-based ML classifier to detect hidden sponsored posts on Twitter and finds 96% of sponsored posts lack disclosure: a measurement exercise, with no indication of a staggered-adoption DiD (article text not available to confirm). (ii) The package stored under this suffix is for another paper (Pandora ad-load RCT with IV and HTE analyses on simulated data), so no data or code for this paper are available.
design_notes: Mismatched package: R lfe::felm IV regressions (sub_norm ~ 1 | 0 | (realizedAdload ~ tg)) and Python HTE notebooks on synthetic data.
data_files_note: No data for the intended paper. Mismatched package ships synthetic data only (ReadMe: data user agreements prevent sharing the original Pandora data).
data_provenance_note: Intended paper's data not shipped; the mismatched package's data are synthetic.
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex abstract (no article text). Lead may want to add this suffix to data/package_mismatches.txt. Eligibility of the intended paper rests on the abstract only; a DiD around a disclosure-policy event cannot be ruled out without the text, but data are unavailable either way.
